**Commentary on Surah "Al-'Asr" (The Declining Day)**, which is Meccan. Qatadah said it is Medinan, and this is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. It has three verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By time,﴾ (1)

There are two issues here.

The first concerns the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿By time (al-'Asr),﴾ meaning "by the age (al-dahr)." This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and others. So *al-'asr* is like *al-dahr*, and from this is the verse of the poet:

*The path of desire is rugged, and the sea of desire is deep...
And the day of desire is a month, and the month of desire is an age.*

That is, an age (*'asr*) by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swears, because of what it contains of admonition through the changing of circumstances and their transformation, and the indication within them of the Maker. It was also said: *al-'asr* means the night and the day. Humayd ibn Thawr said:

*And the two ages will not linger: a day and a night,
When they seek to overtake whatever they aim for.*

The two ages (*al-'asraan*) also means the morning and the evening. He said:

*I delay him through the two ages until he wearies of me,
And he accepts half the debt, though his nose is in the dust.*

He means: when he comes to me at the beginning of the day, I promise him at its end.

It was also said that it is the evening (*al-'ashiyy*), which is the period between the sun's decline and its setting, said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. From this is the verse of the poet:

*Let us go out in the afternoon, O 'Amr, for the 'asr has grown short,
And in the first afternoon outing is the spoil and the reward.*

It is also narrated from Qatadah: it is the last hour of the hours of the day. It was also said: it is an oath by the afternoon prayer (*salat al-'asr*), which is the middle prayer, because it is the best of the prayers; this was said by Muqatil. One says: "The call was made for the 'asr," meaning for the afternoon prayer, and "I prayed the 'asr," meaning the afternoon prayer. In the sound report: [The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer]. Its explanation has already passed in Surah "al-Baqarah" [[see vol. 3, p. 210]]. It was also said: it is an oath by the age of the Prophet ﷺ, for its excellence in the renewal of prophethood within it. It was also said: its meaning is "by the Lord of the 'asr."

The second issue: Malik said: whoever swears that he will not speak to a man for an 'asr, he will not speak to him for a year. Ibn al-'Arabi said: "Malik interpreted the oath of one who swears not to speak to a man for an 'asr as meaning a year, because that is the most that has been said about it, and this is in keeping with his principle of giving a strict meaning in oaths." Al-Shafi'i said: he is fulfilling the oath with an hour, unless he has an intention, and I say likewise, unless the one swearing is an Arab, in which case he is asked: "What did you intend?" If he explains it by something it may bear, it is accepted from him, unless it is the lesser meaning. According to the school of Malik, it would be taken to mean what he explains. And Allah knows best.

This is the answer to the oath. What is meant by "the human being" is the disbeliever, as Ibn 'Abbas said in the narration of Abu Salih. Al-Dahhak narrated from him, saying: He means a group of the polytheists: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza, and al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth. It was also said: by "the human being" is meant the human race in general. "Surely in loss" means: in deception (ghabn). Al-Akhfash said: in destruction (halakah). Al-Farra' said: in punishment ('uqubah), and from this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the consequence of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 9]. Ibn Zayd said: in evil. It was also said: in deficiency; the meanings are close.

It is narrated from Sallam: ﴿By time﴾ with a kasra on the sad (wal-'asri). Al-A'raj, Talhah and 'Isa al-Thaqafi read ﴿khusrin﴾ with a damma on the sin. Harun narrated this from Abu Bakr from 'Asim. The correct form in both cases is assimilation of the vowel (al-itba'). It is said: khusrin and khusurin, like 'usrin and 'usurin. 'Ali used to recite it: ﴿By time, and the vicissitudes of the age, indeed the human being is in loss﴾, and that it remains in it until the end of time. Ibrahim said: indeed the human being, when he is given a long life in this world and becomes decrepit, is in deficiency, weakness and regression, except the believers, for their rewards which they used to do in the time of their youth are recorded for them. Its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature; then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 4-5]. He said: Our recitation is ﴿By time, indeed the human being is in loss, and indeed he is at the end of time﴾. The sound position is what the community and the mushafs agree upon. The refutation of those who opposed the Mushaf of 'Uthman, and that such readings are not Qur'an to be recited, has already passed in the introduction of this book, so consider it there. [See vol. 1, p. 80, second or third edition.]

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 103, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Except those who believe﴾ is an exception from "mankind" (al-insan), since it means "people" (al-nas) according to the sound view.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ means they performed the obligatory duties (al-fara'id al-muftaraḍa) incumbent upon them, and they were the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) "By time," then I said: "What is its tafsir, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "By time" is an oath from Allah; your Lord swore by the latter part of the day. ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾: Abu Jahl. ﴿Except those who believe﴾: Abu Bakr. ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾: Umar. ﴿And advise one another to truth﴾: Uthman. ﴿And advise one another to patience﴾: "Ali," may Allah be pleased with them all. And thus Ibn Abbas delivered a sermon from the pulpit, traced to him (mawquf). The meaning of (wa-tawasaw) is "they loved one another (tahabbu)," advised one another, and urged one another.

(bil-haqq) means "with monotheism (al-tawhid)," as al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas. Qatadah said: "with the truth" means the Qur'an. Al-Suddi said: "the Truth" here is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

(wa-tawasaw bil-sabr) means upon obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and patience in refraining from His disobedience. This has been mentioned previously [[See p. 71 of this part.]]. And Allah knows best.
